long.title: 12 Things You Believe About Your Cat and Dog (Most Are Wrong)
tags: do cats always land on their feet
do dogs see in black and white
long.comment:
📝 SCORE CHECK: how many did you get out of 12? 👇

Answer key: TRUE = nose prints, cats can't taste sweet, dogs understand pointing. Everything else was FALSE.

Which one did your family swear was true? Comment it.
long.description:
TRUE or FALSE? Cats always land on their feet, dogs see in black and white, a dog's mouth is cleaner than yours... 12 pet facts, 3 seconds each. Keep score and drop it in the comments 👇

0:00 Play along
0:18 Cats always land on their feet?
1:08 Dogs only see in black and white?
1:51 A bowl of milk is good for cats?
2:24 A dog's nose print is as unique as a fingerprint?
3:06 Cats only purr when they're happy?
3:51 One dog year equals seven human years?
4:30 Cats can't taste sweet things?
5:06 A wagging tail always means a happy dog?
5:50 Cats are nocturnal?
6:28 Dogs understand when you point at something?
7:05 Dogs eat grass because they feel sick?
7:46 A dog's mouth is cleaner than a human's?
8:23 Scores

Subscribe: next it's how cats domesticated themselves.

shorts.title: Do Cats Always Land on Their Feet? 🐈
shorts.description:
TRUE or FALSE? Cats always land on their feet. Guess before the timer, then comment if you got it right 👇 Full quiz episode on the channel.

#shorts #trueorfalse #animalfacts #quiz

Photos (iNaturalist): House cat: Josiah Londerée (CC BY), Alex Abair (CC BY), Alan Rockefeller (CC BY), Chris Quirin (CC BY). creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
shorts.comment:
Kittens start learning the righting reflex at about three to four weeks old, and have it mostly figured out by about seven weeks.

shorts.comment:
